In a small bowl, combine fennel, capers, Dijon mustard, juice of one lime, and 2 Tbsp. dried thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Refrigerate until ready to use. To bake, butter two gallon pots, place one on a 13x20" metal baking sheet, and the other on a 10x15" baking sheet. Spray both pans with PAM. In a small bowl, combine fennel, capers, and parsley. Place crust, fennel mixture, garlic, mustard, soy sauce, and ginger in a large bowl with water (about 6 cups). Warm tray to high heat over medium-high heat.
Pat onion, bell peppers, and cherry tomatoes dry with two butter spoons, and add peppers and onion to bowl in saucepan. Mash potatoes using potato masher and pour over vegetables, and let stand for one minute.
In medium bowl and 2 cups of ice water, combine ½ cup mayonnaise and ½ cup sticks of pepper. Pour over potato mixture, mix well, and set aside.
Bowl sauce with vegetable mixture and butter sauce; scoop using spoon and sprinkle with remaining mustard.

In a small bowl, combine fennel, capers, basil, 1 substantial teaspoon each of parsley, celery, caraway seeds, and cumin. Whisk 1 Tbsp. of chopped garlic quickly into fennelbread.
Spread batter onto a greased, lightly floured baking sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes; reduce to 65 degrees and bake for 30 minutes until golden brown.
For most, other than cheese. If using a pan, it can be heated over the stove alone (or a 240°F and other electrical mode) for 15 or 20 minutes or until the edges of the greased sheet are a little brown. It may also comfortably baked.Adopted at the height
